Goal: Can MVFA's few-shot inference be made inductive, scoring each image only with statistics of the K normal support images and source-validation data instead of test-set min-max normalisation, while keeping image AUROC within 1 point of the re-run transductive baseline and making each image's score invariant to the composition of the rest of the test set (prevalence 10-50%, with and without outliers)? The replacement is evaluated component by component (normalisation, then fusion weight, then image-level aggregation), with sensitivity at 95% specificity and expected calibration error reported alongside AUROC.

Code-verified facts about the public code of the source paper (github.com/MediaBrain-SJTU/MVFA-AD):
- CLIP/adapter.py: CLIP_Inplanted wraps a frozen CLIP ViT-L/14-336 (input 240x240); ClipAdapter bottleneck adapters are inserted after layers [6, 12, 18, 24]; there are two adapter sets, seg_adapters (segmentation branch) and det_adapters (detection branch), mixed residually with ratio 0.1.
- prompt.py / utils.py: the text side is two frozen text anchors (normal, abnormal) averaged over 35 templates.
- train_zero.py (zero-shot, leave-one-dataset-out): det branch trained with BCE on the MEAN-pooled patch anomaly map for every image; seg branch trained with Focal + Dice on pixel masks only for BrainMRI, LiverCT, RESC; batch size 1; the checkpoint is selected on the target test set.
- train_few.py: few-shot fine-tuning on K normal + K abnormal (masked) images from BMAD's valid/ split, one fixed draw (dataset/fewshot_seed); the checkpoint is selected on the target test set.
- test_few.py: zero-shot map (text similarity) and few-shot map (1 - max cosine to a memory bank of support patch features, per level) are each min-max normalised over the whole test set and added with weight 0.5; image score = max of fused pixel map (masked datasets) or mean-pooled det score (others).
- BMAD: BrainMRI, LiverCT, RESC have masks; OCT17, ChestXray, HIS have image labels only; each has train/valid/test splits.

Required evaluation protocol: Shared evaluation protocol (from limitation group C: G2, G10, G12, G16): checkpoints and hyper-parameters are selected on a held-out validation split of the SOURCE modalities and never on the target test set, and the MVFA baseline is re-run under the same rule; results are reported under a modality-disjoint leave-one-modality-out split (RESC and OCT17 are held out together, never one with the other in training), with patient-level separation where identifiers exist, over at least 3 random seeds and 3 few-shot support draws with mean and standard deviation, and against the missing baselines named in G12 where relevant.
Parent hypotheses: Parent 1:
TITLE: Conformal few-shot p-values and temperature-calibrated zero-shot probabilities fused in log-odds
SUMMARY: Turn the few-shot branch into a conformal p-value from the leave-one-out support distribution, keep the zero-shot branch as a temperature-calibrated probability, and combine both in log-odds with weights fitted on source episodes.
HYPOTHESIS: Fusing a conformal few-shot p-value with a temperature-calibrated zero-shot probability in log-odds keeps image AUROC within 1 point of the transductive pipeline at K >= 4, makes each image's score exactly invariant to the test set, and controls the false-positive rate on normal images at the nominal 5% within 2 points when the few-shot branch alone is thresholded.
RATIONALE: The empirical-CDF parent makes scores test-set-invariant but treats both branches as uncalibrated ranks; the log-odds parent shows that the zero-shot branch is already a probability once a temperature is fitted. The two branches differ in nature: the few-shot score is a distance to supports, for which a rank against leave-one-out support scores is a valid conformal p-value with a finite-sample false-positive guarantee, while the zero-shot score is a classifier output. Treating each by its nature, a p-value for the few-shot branch and a probability for the zero-shot branch, and combining them in log-odds with source-fitted weights preserves the guarantee of the first and the calibration of the second.
METHOD: 1) Few-shot: for each support i, LOO image score r_i (top-1% mean of 1 - max cosine to the bank without i, averaged over levels); test image score s; conformal p = (1 + #{r_i >= s})/(K + 1). 2) Zero-shot: p0 = softmax(T^-1 logits) with T fitted on source validation. 3) Fused logit z = w0 logit(p0) + w1 logit(1 - p) + c, with w0, w1, c fitted by logistic regression on source episodes (50 per source modality, K matched). 4) test_few.py: remove min-max; report thresholded results at p <= 0.05 (few-shot alone) and at z = 0. 5) Pixel maps: the same transform per pixel using LOO pixel reference sets subsampled to 10^5 values. No training.
EXPERIMENT: Leave-one-modality-out on BMAD (RESC and OCT17 held out together), MVFA retrained with source-validation selection; K in {2,4,8,16}; 3 seeds x 3 support draws. Baselines: transductive MVFA pipeline, support z-score. Ordered ablation: (i) conformal few-shot alone, (ii) + calibrated zero-shot with average fusion, (iii) log-odds fusion with source weights. Metrics: image/pixel AUROC, realised FPR at p <= 0.05, ECE, score shift under resampling. Falsified if AUROC drops more than 1 point or realised FPR at nominal 5% exceeds 7%.

Parent 2:
TITLE: Level-wise conformal p-values combined with the Cauchy rule and calibrated isotonically
SUMMARY: Compute a conformal p-value for each MVFA feature level and branch from leave-one-out support scores, combine the eight dependent p-values with the Cauchy combination test, and map the result to a probability with a source-fitted isotonic map.
HYPOTHESIS: Cauchy combination of eight level-wise conformal p-values keeps image AUROC within 1 point of the transductive pipeline, gives a realised false-positive rate within 2 points of the nominal 5% despite the strong dependence between levels, and after isotonic calibration reaches ECE at least 40% lower than the CDF-average parent.
RATIONALE: The CDF parent averages branch CDFs, which ignores that averaging dependent ranks is not a valid test; the conformal parent uses a single fused few-shot score and loses level-specific evidence. MVFA's four adapter levels and two branches give eight correlated views of each image. The Cauchy combination test (Liu and Xie, 2020) combines dependent p-values into one whose tail is approximately exact under arbitrary dependence, so level-wise conformal p-values can be combined without modelling their correlation, preserving false-positive control. An isotonic map on the combined statistic then supplies calibrated probabilities.
METHOD: 1) For level l and branch b: LOO support image scores r_i^{bl} (top-1% mean of that level's map); test score s^{bl}; p_bl = (1 + #{r_i >= s})/(K + 1). For the zero-shot branch the support score is the softmax abnormal probability map at that level. 2) Cauchy statistic T = (1/8) sum tan((0.5 - p_bl) pi); combined p = 0.5 - arctan(T)/pi. 3) Isotonic map from -log p to probability fitted on source episodes. 4) test_few.py: implement; remove test-set min-max. No adapter training.
EXPERIMENT: Leave-one-modality-out on BMAD (RESC and OCT17 held out together), MVFA retrained with source-validation selection; K in {2,4,8,16}; 3 seeds x 3 support draws. Baselines: transductive MVFA pipeline, support z-score. Ordered ablation: (i) single fused conformal p-value, (ii) level-wise Cauchy combination, (iii) Fisher combination (assumes independence, expected to be anti-conservative), (iv) + isotonic calibration. Metrics: realised FPR at 0.05, image AUROC, ECE, score shift under resampling. Falsified if Cauchy-combined FPR exceeds 7% or AUROC drops more than 1 point.
